verification_note: Full real-execution verification (dotnet 10.0.401 is available per the playbook's environment note). Cloned the repository at the exact pinned source_revision into an isolated scratchpad directory, added a throwaway probe console app with a ProjectReference to src/main/Aspose.ThreeD/Aspose.ThreeD.csproj, and ran Scene.Save() against every format extension the README's opening paragraph / Key Capabilities / At-a-Glance diagram / Scope-and-Limitations claim as supported. This is not code-reading-only verification for this repository, unlike the Java/TypeScript siblings in this batch.

facts.claim: NuGet package Aspose.3D.FOSS is at version 26.1.0, dotnet add package Aspose.3D.FOSS --version 26.1.0 is correct
facts.evidence: src/main/Aspose.ThreeD/Aspose.ThreeD.csproj: <Version>26.1.0</Version>, <PackageId>Aspose.3D.FOSS</PackageId> (read directly via GitHub Contents API at source_revision).

facts.claim: Library targets net6.0, net8.0, net10.0, and netcoreapp3.1 in Release builds

facts.evidence: Aspose.ThreeD.csproj has zero <PackageReference> entries (only a <None> pack item for the README/logo).

facts.claim: (derived from code, not a direct README quote) Scene.Save(string)/Scene.Open(string) both resolve a format solely through FileFormat.GetFormatByExtension(), which only recognizes extensions present in the private static FileFormat._formats list
facts.evidence: FileFormat.cs: GetFormatByExtension() loops over the private static List<FileFormat> _formats and throws ArgumentException("Unsupported file format: {ext}") if no entry matches; InitializeFormats() populates _formats with exactly 8 entries (the internal nested ObjFormat/StlFormat/GltfFormat/FbxFormat/Microsoft3MFFormat/ColladaFormat/PlyFormat/Discreet3DSFormat classes). Scene.Save(string fileName) and Scene.Open(string fileName) both call FileFormat.GetFormatByExtension(Path.GetExtension(fileName)) before ever reaching IOService.

facts.claim: The opening paragraph, Key Capabilities, and At-a-Glance diagram claim Scene can read/write U3D (Universal 3D) and that the library can convert '...plus Microsoft 3MF and AVEVA PDMS RVM models, AMF, and an HTML5/Aspose 3D Web viewer export'; the At-a-Glance diagram lists RVM and U3D as both inputs (i1/i3) and outputs (o1/o3), and AMF/HTML5 as output o4
facts.evidence: Reproduced live by cloning the repo at this exact source_revision, building a throwaway console app referencing Aspose.ThreeD.csproj directly (dotnet 10.0.401), and calling scene.Save(path) for each extension: .rvm -> ArgumentException: Unsupported file format: .rvm; .u3d -> ArgumentException: Unsupported file format: .u3d; .amf -> ArgumentException: Unsupported file format: .amf; .html -> ArgumentException: Unsupported file format: .html. Root cause confirmed by code reading (F-DISPATCH-GATEKEEPER): FileFormat.RvmText/RvmBinary (Formats.RvmFormat), FileFormat.Universal3D, FileFormat.AMF, and FileFormat.HTML5/Aspose3DWeb are all declared as public static readonly fields on FileFormat, giving the clear visual impression of registered, dispatchable formats, but none of them is added to the private _formats list that GetFormatByExtension actually searches. No RVM/U3D/AMF/HTML5 reader or writer class exists anywhere in the repository (confirmed via a recursive tree search for file names matching rvm|u3d|amf|html5 -- only option-class stub files exist: RvmLoadOptions.cs/RvmSaveOptions.cs, U3dLoadOptions.cs/U3dSaveOptions.cs, AmfSaveOptions.cs, Html5SaveOptions.cs; no RvmReader/RvmWriter/U3dReader/U3dWriter/AmfWriter/Html5Writer file exists, and no test file for any of these four formats exists in src/test/). These four formats are completely non-functional through the only entry point the README documents (Scene.Save()/Scene.Open()), not partially degraded.

facts.claim: Scope and Limitations' own text: 'RvmFormat.LoadAttributes is not implemented -- core RVM geometry import/export works, RVM attribute data does not load'
facts.evidence: Same evidence as F-RVM-U3D-AMF-HTML5-UNREACHABLE: RVM 'core geometry import/export' does not work at all -- Scene.Save/Open never even reach RvmFormat-specific code because GetFormatByExtension(".rvm") throws first. The live text's self-disclosed limitation is itself wrong: it understates the defect (implies ~90% working, only metadata missing) when the true state is 0% functional through the public API.

Same live probe run: scene.Save() for .obj/.stl/.3mf/.dae/.ply/.3ds all completed without exception and produced non-empty files, for a scene built the exact way the README's own Quick Start example builds one (Box primitive + LambertMaterial attached via RootNode.CreateChildNode). Notably, unlike this product family's Python sibling (aspose-3d-foss/Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-Python, see evidence/build/P1_VERTICAL_SLICE), OBJ export and COLLADA export both work correctly here -- this is a genuinely separate codebase/platform and its defects (or lack thereof) do not transfer from the Python findings.

facts.claim: Microsoft3MFFormat's build-instruction metadata (IsBuildable, GetTransformForBuild, SetBuildable, object type accessors) is not implemented -- core 3MF geometry import/export works, production-extension metadata does not
facts.evidence: Read Formats/Microsoft3MFFormat.cs directly: IsBuildable/GetTransformForBuild/SetBuildable/SetObjectType/GetObjectType all unconditionally throw NotImplementedException. Separately, core 3MF geometry import/export is confirmed working via the live probe (F-OBJ-STL-3MF-DAE-PLY-3DS-EXPORT-WORK) -- Scene.Save("x.3mf") succeeds because the *dispatched* internal Aspose.ThreeD.Microsoft3MFFormat class (added to _formats, backed by a real Microsoft3MFReader/Microsoft3MFWriter) is a distinct type from the public Aspose.ThreeD.Formats.Microsoft3MFFormat metadata-stub class exposed as FileFormat.Microsoft3MF -- both claims in this README bullet are independently true and not in tension with each other.

facts.claim: PLY import and export both work through Scene.Open()/Scene.Save(); the confusable PlyFormat class exposed as FileFormat.PLY is a separate, non-dispatched type whose own Encode/Decode methods do throw NotImplementedException
facts.evidence: Confirmed by the live probe (Scene.Save("x.ply") succeeds) plus code reading: the dispatched PlyFormat (internal, in FileFormat.cs, added to _formats) is backed by real PlyReader/PlyWriter classes used by IOService.CreateImporter/CreateExporter; the separate public Formats.PlyFormat class exposed as FileFormat.PLY has Encode()/Decode() methods that all throw NotImplementedException("PLY encoding/decoding not implemented in FOSS version") -- exactly the same dual-class pattern the README's own Scope and Limitations section already discloses accurately for PLY, in contrast to its inaccurate disclosure for RVM.

facts.claim: PdfFormat and DracoFormat have no reader/writer implementation anywhere in the codebase -- PDF and Google Draco import/export are genuinely not functional
facts.evidence: Read Formats/DracoFormat.cs and Formats/PdfFormat.cs directly: every method (Decode/Encode for Draco; Extract/ExtractScene for Pdf) unconditionally throws NotImplementedException. Neither format appears in FileFormat._formats, consistent with the README's own claim.

facts.claim: dotnet test src/test/Aspose.ThreeD.Tests/Aspose.ThreeD.Tests.csproj runs the test suite
facts.evidence: The project path was confirmed to exist in the repository tree listing, but the full test suite was not executed this session (only a standalone probe console app referencing the library directly was built and run, which was sufficient to answer the format-dispatch question above within the ~15-20 minute budget).
